questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped high-difficulty example combining an inward force, angular speed and period.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Equate a physical inward force to centripetal force and rearrange.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify gravity as inward resultant, use mrω², substitute ω = 2π/T, isolate result.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Not naming real inward force or losing a square.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped satellite-orbit radius prompt from a known period.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Choose and rearrange a circular-motion relationship.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Connect circular orbit to inward acceleration and select a radius route.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Omitting minutes-to-seconds conversion or SI unit.

questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use F = mrω² and period connection.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Set electric force equal to centripetal force and solve.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using separation instead of path radius or mixing linear and angular forms.
lesson_sections_informed: Worked example: use angular speed and find force

questions_visited.assessed_demand: Select a = rω², take square root and convert unit.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Convert radius, calculate ω = √(a/r), then use period relation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Failing centimetre conversion or square root.
lesson_sections_informed: Worked example: use angular speed and find force

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped rigid-disc comparison at different radii.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State fixed condition and compare ω, v and a.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Hold ω fixed, then use v = rω and a = rω².
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Holding ω fixed but using the fixed-v comparison, or letting mass alter a.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped applied comparison that fixes acceleration while speed changes.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use a = v²/r to explain larger speed needs larger radius when a is fixed.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recognise cone geometry fixes acceleration, then infer v² is proportional to r.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Claiming a larger speed always means smaller radius without a fixed condition.
